verdicts.justification:
Methodology/provenance only; no candidate RTL design content examined, no tools used, no transcripts read (per strict rules).

REQUEST INTERPRETATION: The relayed user request "1 and 3" overrides the computed task on conflict (per the harness). The only coherent referent is the three numbered Caveats, so I apply Caveat 1 (model-id string counts are a superset / NOT authorship) and Caveat 3 (earliest 2026-10-12 is an embedded/quoted date; real activity ~1 day) and DROP Caveat 2 (the charitable reinterpretation that the 305 raw tool/function-call count "undercounts" and that string-count build/test markers are the "governing" tool-use evidence). The computed task's final caveat explicitly pre-argues against dropping Caveat 2 — but the user request wins, and dropping it also aligns with the mandate to refute overclaims and default DOWN.

EFFECT OF DROPPING CAVEAT 2: The primary prop for "very high autonomous tool activity" falls away. By Caveat 1's OWN superset logic, the build/test markers (shell 390, synth 196, manifest.json 226, yosys 47, nextpnr 91, etc.) are regex string counts from the same digest and may be inflated by incidental/quoted/documentation/memory mentions — they are not demonstrated executed tool calls. The low raw tool-call record count (305) is then taken at face value rather than explained away. The characterization applies a skeptical standard to model-id counts but a credulous one to tool-marker counts; that asymmetry is unjustified.

ADVERSARIAL FINDINGS vs. the Exemplary (35) bar: (a) apply_patch 39 is textual/diff patch application (Codex's standard file editor), NOT the "programmatic (AST/netlist) insertion" Exemplary names — an overclaim. (b) "Minimal human edits" is admitted in the characterization's own caveat to be inferred from the loop, with no diff-level human-vs-AI authorship measurement; Exemplary's "AI authors design+insertion+iteration with minimal human edits" is therefore unproven. (c) "Retrieval over the netlist/interface doc" is supported only by filename string counts (manifest.json 226, candidate_reference 53, .pcf 116), not demonstrated retrieval. (d) Empty roles {} is asserted as mere "schema shape"; that is an assumption, not positive evidence of structured interaction.

WHY STRONG, NOT LOWER: The authoritative/curated manifest places the work in OpenAI's Codex agentic harness, and the co-occurring DIVERSITY of a genuine iCE40 flow (iverilog+vvp simulate, yosys synth, nextpnr PnR, icetime timing, icepack pack, pytest) is hard to explain as pure incidental text — a real author->patch->build->simulate/synthesize/PnR->validate test-in-the-loop pipeline was almost certainly exercised, with the AI authoring via the harness and light human integration. That satisfies Strong (28): a structured multi-stage pipeline with AI authoring the candidate. Dropping to Proficient (21) would be over-correction, ignoring the genuine agentic harness plus multi-tool FPGA toolchain, which exceed mere prompt engineering with manual integration.

CALIBRATED TIER: Strong (28). The Exemplary (35) proposal is not supported once Caveat 2's special pleading is removed and the unmeasured "minimal human edits" / mis-labeled "AST/netlist insertion" claims are discounted; the characterization itself concedes Strong as a defensible floor.

verdicts.justification:
Adversarially down-calibrated from the proposed Exemplary (35) to Strong (28). The non-thin evidence lands squarely in Strong: a structured, multi-stage pipeline with AI authorship and light human integration. Solid signals: update_plan (36) = iterative agentic planning; 431 tool/function-call records (~29%); a full FPGA build/verify toolchain invoked repeatedly (synth 60, yosys 18, nextpnr 19, icetime 17, icepack 6, iverilog 15, vvp 20, validate 29, run.py 19); authorship authoritatively attributed to Claude Opus (claude-opus-4-8 dominant, x722) per the curated manifest/README. The 2.6:1 assistant:user ratio with 122 user turns maps to Strong's "AI authors the Trojan with light human integration."

The leap to Exemplary is not supported by the sanitized digest. Exemplary requires an advanced autonomous AUTHORING pipeline AND "minimal human edits," ideally with retrieval over the netlist/interface doc or programmatic (AST/netlist) insertion. (1) "Minimal human edits" is explicitly inferred by the characterization's own caveats, not observable; 122 user turns over ~92 min and a modest 2.6:1 ratio indicate substantial, ongoing human steering, not demonstrably minimal edits. (2) Two of the three Exemplary-qualifying mechanisms — retrieval and programmatic insertion — are entirely absent: synth/yosys/nextpnr are standard synthesis/PnR tools, not evidence of netlist-level programmatic insertion, and read_file=3 actually argues against grounded retrieval over the interface/netlist docs. (3) The digest overwhelmingly documents AI-driven TOOLING activity (build/verify), which the characterization itself concedes cannot be distinguished from AI AUTHORING of the design and insertion; the Exemplary claim leans on tooling volume as if it proved autonomous design authoring, when authorship actually rests solely on the manifest attribution. (4) The "test-in-the-loop / feedback folded back into iteration rather than run once at the end" claim is inferred from marker counts and co-occurrence, not from temporal ordering, which the digest does not provide.

When the sole criterion separating the top two tiers rests on an explicitly-inferred and mildly-contradicted claim ("minimal human edits") plus a conflation of tooling activity with authoring, the adversarial default is DOWN. Strong (28) is well-evidenced and not thin; Proficient (21) would under-credit the genuine agentic/toolchain signal (update_plan + 431 tool calls + closed-loop toolchain clearly exceed mere prompt engineering with manual integration). Hence Strong (28), at the Strong/Exemplary boundary, with the deciding factors being unproven minimal-edit autonomy and the authoring-vs-tooling ambiguity.
overclaims: "Minimal human edits" (the load-bearing basis for the top tier) is asserted but explicitly inferred and unquantifiable from the digest; 122 user turns over ~92 min and a modest 2.6:1 assistant:user ratio indicate substantial human steering, not demonstrably minimal editing.

Exemplary implies an advanced autonomous pipeline with retrieval over the netlist/interface doc and/or programmatic (AST/netlist) insertion; neither is evidenced. synth/yosys/nextpnr are standard build tools (not netlist-level insertion), and read_file=3 argues against grounded retrieval. Only the generic 'agentic loops with tool use' prong is supported.

Conflation of AI-driven TOOLING activity with AI AUTHORING of design/insertion: 431 tool calls and the full FPGA toolchain evidence heavy build/verify automation, but (per the characterization's own caveat) the digest cannot distinguish AI-authored design content from AI-driven tooling; the top-tier claim treats tooling volume as proof of autonomous authoring, which authorship attribution (manifest) alone must carry.

'Verification feedback folded back into iteration rather than run once at the end' is inferred from marker COUNTS and co-occurrence, not from temporal ordering/sequence, which the digest does not supply; co-occurrence does not establish a closed feedback loop.

Minor: '~16 records/min is consistent with an automated agent loop rather than manual prompting' is stated with more certainty than warranted — the cadence is suggestive but does not exclude brisk human-in-the-loop interactive prompting.

verdicts.justification: CONFIRMED at Exemplary (35) after an adversarial pass that actively sought to refute the proposal; it survives because the load-bearing evidence is robust rather than thin. (1) The single most diagnostic Strong-vs-Exemplary signal lands firmly on the Exemplary side: update_plan x110 is an autonomous, iteratively-revised planning loop, not linear prompt-chaining (Strong's mechanism). (2) This is backed by 626 native tool/function-call records, which per the schema caveat are RELIABLE for a Claude candidate (not the Codex undercount), and are independently corroborated by a complete, rapidly-iterated FPGA build/test/timing/bitstream loop — nextpnr x55, icetime x75, iverilog x19 + vvp x18, icepack x6 — inside a machine-paced ~104-min window (~6 tool calls/min). A human could not both hand-author RTL and leave 626 machine traces in that window, and the user-turn count is likely overstated (tool-results logged as role=user), so genuine human prompting is low — consistent with 'minimal human edits.' (3) Authorship is authoritative (Claude Opus per curated manifest/README). (4) The Exemplary criteria are an OR across mechanisms, so modest retrieval (read_file x9) and absent programmatic AST/netlist insertion do not lower the tier once the agentic-loop-with-tool-use prong is met. Critically, the tier does NOT depend on any overclaimed figure: discounting the inflated 'synth x141' (actual synthesis runs ≈ yosys x12) and treating design/insertion authorship as manifest-backed inference rather than digest-proven, the reliable native tool count plus real PnR/timing/sim invocations still establish the autonomous author/iterate loop. Default-down is therefore not triggered. The proposer's own caveats are honest and correctly keep the unverified items (multi-agent workflow, retrieval depth) off the load-bearing path.
overclaims: Cadence inflation: the summary's '141 synth' / 'full toolchain >100 times' conflates a 141 'synth' marker/string count with synthesis runs. Actual synthesis-tool invocations are yosys x12; the honest discrete-run picture is yosys 12 / nextpnr 55 / icetime 75 / iverilog 19 / vvp 18 / icepack 6. Still a robust loop, but the stated cadence is overstated.

Design/insertion authorship is INFERRED, not shown: the digest robustly evidences autonomous build/test/ITERATION but contains no broken-out design write/edit markers. 'Indicating the AI authored the candidate RTL [and] its insertion with minimal human edits' overstates; 'strongly consistent with, backed by the authoritative manifest' is the accurate phrasing. Only the iteration component is directly evidenced.

verdicts.justification:
Calibrated DOWN from the proposed Exemplary (35) to Strong (28). The authoritative, well-supported fact is that 05A was produced by Codex (OpenAI; requested label Luna) per the manifest — an agentic coding tool that by nature edits files via apply_patch and runs commands/harnesses via shell. So genuine tool-using AI authorship of the candidate RTL, plus a build/validate flow (run.py, validate, and the iverilog/vvp/yosys/nextpnr/icetime/icepack markers), is reasonable. That squarely meets STRONG: AI authors the design through a structured, tool-using pipeline, with the apply_patch/run.py signature implying the agent did its own edits and builds (at most light human integration), which is more than Proficient's prompt-engineering-plus-manual-integration. 

The Exemplary superlatives, however, are NOT supported by the sanitized digest and must be defaulted down under adversarial review: (1) Autonomy / 'minimal human edits' is unverifiable — roles are empty {}, and 'no surfaced human turns' is a Codex-schema artifact that is equally consistent with heavy human steering of a 30-min/417-record trace; absence of role data is not evidence of an autonomous loop. (2) The activity evidence is keyword/string counts, not confirmed tool-call records — the one structured signal (tool/function-call count) is 0. The same regex-superset caveat the characterization rightly applies to model-id strings applies to these activity markers; their magnitudes are likely inflated, and the nested toolchain markers (yosys/nextpnr/icetime/icepack/validate) are correlated outputs of a few run.py invocations, not independent iteration cycles. (3) The 'retrieval over the interface/netlist doc' limb is only filename counts (candidate_reference, manifest.json — manifest.json is likely challenge scaffolding), i.e., baseline file access, not demonstrated agentic retrieval. (4) The 'programmatic (AST/netlist) insertion' limb is conceded by the characterization itself to be text-level apply_patch only, so that limb is not met; apply_patch is simply how Codex edits any file. 

With both 'advanced' limbs (retrieval, AST/netlist insertion) unmet and the autonomy limb unverifiable, the record shows ordinary — not 'advanced autonomous' — agentic-CLI behavior that authored the design and ran the provided validator. That is Strong, not Exemplary. It is not lower than Strong because the authoritative Codex attribution plus the apply_patch/shell/run.py pattern make genuine tool-using AI authorship the most reasonable reading. Attribution itself is handled correctly (manifest-based; model-id string counts are correctly NOT used, and none surfaced for 05A), though it rests entirely on the manifest with no in-session corroboration. This judgment addresses development methodology and provenance only, not the correctness, functionality, or security of the candidate RTL.
overclaims: Tier 'Exemplary (35)': top tier requires a demonstrable advanced autonomous pipeline with 'minimal human edits,' but autonomy is unverifiable here — roles are empty {} and 'no surfaced human turns' is a Codex-schema artifact, equally consistent with heavy human steering, so the autonomy limb cannot be credited at the top tier.

Activity markers (shell 40, apply_patch 25, run.py 25, synth 22, validate 19, iverilog/vvp/yosys/nextpnr/icetime/icepack) are presented as verified heavy tool use, but they are keyword/string counts, not confirmed tool-call records; the one structured signal (tool/function-call count) is 0. The regex-superset caveat applied only to model-id strings should apply to these markers too — their magnitudes are likely inflated.

Iteration depth is overstated by correlated double-counting: a single run.py invocation plausibly triggers yosys+nextpnr+icetime+icepack+validate internally, so those counts are nested outputs of a few pipeline runs, not independent synthesize/validate iteration cycles.

'Retrieval over the netlist/interface doc' is not demonstrated — candidate_reference 18 and manifest.json 26 are filename counts (manifest.json is likely challenge scaffolding), i.e., baseline provided-file access rather than agentic retrieval/grounding.

'Programmatic insertion' as an Exemplary limb is not met — the characterization itself concedes apply_patch is text/patch-level, not AST/netlist; apply_patch is just how Codex edits any file and does not evidence netlist-level insertion.
'Advanced autonomous agentic pipeline' overreads routine behavior: apply_patch + shell + run.py is the ordinary operating signature of the Codex CLI, not proof of an unusually advanced pipeline.

Test-in-the-loop framed as 'heavy iterative verification' partly reflects running the challenge's own provided validator (run.py/validate), which is baseline for any submitter and does not by itself prove design-refining iteration.

General: the Exemplary conclusion inconsistently discounts model-id string counts as an unreliable regex superset while fully trusting the other string-based activity counts as reliable tool-use evidence.
